newsitem.title: USA: Northeast has interim credit agreement.
newsitem.headline: Northeast has interim credit agreement.

text.p: Northeast Utilities reached an interim agreement on a bank credit line last week, spokesman Jeffrey R. Kotkin told Reuters Wednesday.

Commenting on "the new credit agreement" due to expire March 28 reported in the company's 10K, he said that agreement was extended for two weeks, then replaced with an interim agreement with 12 banks led by Citicorp, Fleet Financial Group Inc and Toronto-Dominion Bank.
Koktin said the agreement, which is good through May, provides a $190 million credit line, adding Northeast has "zero borrowed" under the agreement.
By the end of May the company "hopes to have regulatory approval" for its agreement with the banks, which will provide a $314 million credit line, Kotin said.
The 10K also said Northeast Utilities' operating income to interest expense ratio was 0.87 to one on December 31 and its common equity ratio was 34.4 percent.

It put the company's 1997 financing requirements at $621 million, including $374 million for Connecticut Light & Power Co, $60 million for Public Service Co of New Hampshire, $53 million for Western Massachusetts Electric Co and $44 million for North Atlantic Energy Corp.
"The system companies generally proposed to finance their 1997 requirements through internally generated funds and short-term borrowings," the 10K continued.

The Management's Discussion and Analysis portion of Northeast's annual report, which was attached to the 10K, noted the system had about $200 million of cash as of December 31, mostly as a result of two CL&P bond issues. It noted one of these was issued in anticipation of the maturity of about $193 million of bonds in April.

It also said CL&P and Western Massachusetts had established facilities under which they may sell up to $200 million and $40 million, respectively, of their billed and unbilled accounts receivable. As of February 21, $10 and $15 million, respectively, had been sold.

It said management believes the borrowing facilities in place provide the system with access to the funds needed to bring the Millstone nuclear power plant back to service if the units begin operations close to previously projected schedules.
